main.desc: Mass shooting and hostage taking in Moscow, Russia

Islamist militants massacred at least 162 while injuring and kidnapping dozens in two villages in Kwara State, Nigeria.

main.desc: Massacre by Terrorist militants in Nigeria

Emperor Taizu (pictured) came to power, initiating the Song dynasty of China that eventually lasted for more than three centuries.
Zhao Kuangyin declares himself Emperor Taizu of Song, ending the Later Zhou and beginning the Song dynasty.
A strong earthquake struck the eastern coast of Sicily, causing at least 15,000 deaths.
A strong earthquake strikes the Ionian coast of Sicily, causing tens of thousands of injuries and deaths, especially in Catania.

events.text: Bartolomeu Dias landed in Mossel Bay, becoming the first European known to have sailed around the Cape of Good Hope, the southern tip of Africa, beginning Portuguese influence and trade in the Indian Ocean.

John Rogers is burned at the stake, becoming the first English Protestant martyr under Queen Mary I.
In Edo (now Tokyo), all but one of the Forty-seven Ronin commit seppuku (ritual suicide) as recompense for avenging their master's death.
The city of Macapá in Brazil is founded by Sebastião Veiga Cabral.
George Washington is unanimously elected as the first President of the United States by the U.S. Electoral College.

main.desc: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1789 to 1797

The Riobamba earthquake, the most powerful in Ecuador's history, devastated Riobamba and many other cities, causing at least 6,000 casualties.

John Marshall, whose court opinions helped lay the basis for U.S. constitutional law and made the Supreme Court a coequal branch of government, took office as chief justice.

main.desc: 1810 invasion of the Caribbean campaign of 1803–1810

main.desc: Branch of the Chilean Armed Forces

events.text: The Ohio Legislature authorizes the construction of the Ohio and Erie Canal and the Miami and Erie Canal.

main.desc: Legislative branch of the state government of Ohio

events.text: The first Mormon pioneers make their exodus from Nauvoo, Illinois, westward towards Salt Lake Valley.
Constantin von Tischendorf rediscovered the Codex Sinaiticus, a 4th-century great uncial codex of the Bible in Greek, in Saint Catherine's Monastery, Egypt.
The Codex Sinaiticus is discovered in Egypt.
American Civil War: In Montgomery, Alabama, delegates from six breakaway U.S. states meet and initiate the process that would form the Confederate States of America on February 8.
The Philippine–American War began when an American soldier, under orders to keep insurgents away from his unit's encampment, fired on a Filipino soldier in Manila.
The Philippine–American War begins when four Filipino soldiers enter the "American Zone" in Manila, igniting the Battle of Manila.
Second Sino-Japanese War: Harbin, Manchuria, falls to Japan.
Adolf Hitler appoints himself as head of the Armed Forces High Command.
The United Service Organization (USO) is created to entertain American troops.

links.t: List of Japanese-run internment camps during World War II

events.text: World War II: Santo Tomas Internment Camp is liberated from Japanese authority.
World War II: The Yalta Conference between the "Big Three" (Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin) opens at the Livadia Palace in the Crimea.

main.desc: 1945 WWII allied discussion of postwar reorganization

events.text: World War II: The British Indian Army and Imperial Japanese Army begin a series of battles known as the Battle of Pokoku and Irrawaddy River operations.

links.t: Battle of Pokoku and Irrawaddy River operations

events.text: Ceylon (later renamed Sri Lanka) becomes independent within the British Commonwealth.

main.desc: British dominion in Asia from 1948 to 1972

events.text: The Angolan War of Independence and the greater Portuguese Colonial War begin.
All Nippon Airways Flight 60 plunges into Tokyo Bay, killing 133.
Lunar Orbiter program: Lunar Orbiter 3 lifts off from Cape Canaveral's Launch Complex 13 on its mission to identify possible landing sites for the Surveyor and Apollo spacecraft.

main.desc: Series of five uncrewed lunar orbiter missions

events.text: Yasser Arafat (pictured) was elected chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization.
American newspaper heiress and socialite Patty Hearst was kidnapped by the Symbionese Liberation Army, which she later joined.
The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army bombed a motor coach carrying off-duty British Armed Forces personnel and their family members, killing twelve people.
The Symbionese Liberation Army kidnaps Patty Hearst in Berkeley, California.

M62 coach bombing: The Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) explodes a bomb on a bus carrying off-duty British Armed Forces personnel in Yorkshire, England. Nine soldiers and three civilians are killed.
Haicheng earthquake (magnitude 7.3 on the Richter scale) occurs in Haicheng, Liaoning, China.
In Guatemala and Honduras an earthquake kills more than 22,000.
A Chicago Transit Authority elevated train rear-ends another and derails, killing 11 and injuring 180, the worst accident in the agency's history.
A coup d'état is led by Hugo Chávez against Venezuelan President Carlos Andrés Pérez.
En route to Lebanon, two Israeli Sikorsky CH-53 troop-transport helicopters collide in mid-air over northern Galilee, Israel, killing 73.
The Bojnurd earthquake measuring Mw 6.5 strikes Iran. With a Mercalli intensity of VIII, it kills at least 88 and damages 173 villages.
An earthquake registering 5.9 MW struck northern Afghanistan, triggering landslides that killed over 2,300 people and destroyed around 15,000 homes.
The 5.9 Mw Afghanistan earthquake shakes the Takhar Province with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII (Very strong). With 2,323 killed, and 818 injured, damage is considered extreme.
Four plain-clothes New York City police officers shot and killed Amadou Diallo, an unarmed 23-year-old immigrant from Guinea, prompting outrage both in and outside the city.
The Philippine-flagged freighter New Carissa ran aground near Coos Bay, Oregon, causing one of the worst oil spills in the state's history.
Unarmed West African immigrant Amadou Diallo is shot 19 times by four plainclothes New York City police officers on an unrelated stake-out, inflaming race relations in the city.

main.desc: 1999 police shooting of a Guinean-American man

events.text: The World Summit Against Cancer for the New Millennium, Charter of Paris is signed by the President of France, Jacques Chirac and the Director General of UNESCO, Koichiro Matsuura, initiating World Cancer Day which is held on February 4 every year.
The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia adopts a new constitution, becoming a loose confederacy between Montenegro and Serbia.
Facebook, a mainstream online social networking site, is founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin.

main.desc: Social networking service owned by Meta Platforms

events.text: The London low emission zone (sign pictured), charging certain diesel-powered commercial vehicles to enter Greater London, came into operation.
Civic mobilizations in Colombia against FARC, under the name A million voices against the FARC.
Shortly after takeoff from Taipei Songshan Airport, the crew of TransAsia Airways Flight 235 shut down the wrong engine in response to a flameout, leading to a crash that resulted in 43 deaths.
TransAsia Airways Flight 235, with 58 people on board, en route from the Taiwanese capital Taipei to Kinmen, crashes into the Keelung River just after takeoff, killing 43 people.
The COVID-19 pandemic causes all casinos in Macau to be closed down for 15 days.
Ten people are killed in a mass shooting at an adult education centre in Örebro, Sweden.
Caesar Augustus is granted the title pater patriae by the Roman Senate.

main.desc: Roman emperor from 27 BC to AD 14

events.text: Pompeii was severely damaged by a strong earthquake, which may have been a precursor to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius that destroyed the town 17 years later.

links.t: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

events.text: An earthquake with an estimated intensity between IX or X on the Mercalli scale occurs in Pompeii, Italy.
An Lushan proclaims himself Emperor of China, founding the short-lived state of Yan.
Pope Clement IV is elected as the 183rd Bishop of Rome and head of the Catholic Church.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1265 to 1268

events.text: Henry of Navarre abjures Catholicism at Tours and rejoins the Protestant forces in the French Wars of Religion.

As part of enforcing Toyotomi Hideyoshi's ban on Christianity in Japan, twenty-six Catholics, a mix of European missionaries and Japanese converts, were executed (depicted) near Nagasaki by crucifixion and impalement.

main.desc: Military ruler of Japan from 1585 to 1598

events.text: A group of early Japanese Christians are killed by the new government of Japan for being seen as a threat to Japanese society.
The first of five strong earthquakes hit the region of Calabria on the Italian Peninsula, killing more than 32,000 people over a period of nearly two months.
In Calabria, a sequence of strong earthquakes begins.
Peninsular War: Siege of Cádiz begins.
Charles XIV John (pictured) succeeded to the thrones of Sweden and Norway as the first monarch of the House of Bernadotte.

main.desc: King of Sweden and Norway from 1818 to 1844

main.desc: King of Sweden and Norway from 1818 to 1844

events.text: The New Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg, Russia, one of the largest and oldest museums in the world, opens to the public.

Alexandru Ioan Cuza, Prince of Moldavia, is also elected as prince of Wallachia, joining the two principalities as a personal union called the United Principalities, an autonomous region within the Ottoman Empire, which ushered in the birth of the modern Romanian state.

main.desc: First ruler of the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (1820–1873)

links.t: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

events.text: In a speech before the U.S. Congress, Representative John Edward Bouligny refused to join his fellow Louisiana congressmen in heeding the state's secession convention and resigning.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

events.text: Prospectors in Moliagul, Australia, discovered the largest alluvial gold nugget ever found, known as the Welcome Stranger.
The largest alluvial gold nugget in history, called the "Welcome Stranger", is found in Moliagul, Victoria, Australia.

main.desc: Loose soil or sediment that is eroded and redeposited in a non-marine setting

events.text: King Leopold II of Belgium establishes the Congo as a personal possession.

main.desc: King of the Belgians from 1865 to 1909

events.text: J. P. Morgan incorporates U.S. Steel in the state of New Jersey, although the company would not start doing business until February 25 and the assets of Andrew Carnegie's Carnegie Steel Company, Elbert H. Gary's Federal Steel Company, and William Henry Moore's National Steel Company were not acquired until April 1.

main.desc: American financier, banker, and art collector (1837–1913)

events.text: In Mexico, the General Hospital of Mexico is inaugurated, initially with four basic specialties.
Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland announces the creation of Bakelite, the world's first synthetic plastic.
Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland announced his invention of Bakelite (production device pictured), the world's first synthetic plastic.
Claudio Monteverdi's last opera, L'incoronazione di Poppea, was performed theatrically for the first time in more than 250 years.
Greek military aviators Michael Moutoussis and Aristeidis Moraitinis perform the first naval air mission in history, with a Farman MF.7 hydroplane.

main.desc: Air warfare branch of Greece's military

events.text: Claudio Monteverdi's last opera L'incoronazione di Poppea was performed theatrically for the first time in more than 250 years.
The U.S. Congress overrode President Woodrow Wilson's veto to pass the Immigration Act of 1917, establishing new restrictions on immigrants, including the wholesale ban of people from much of Asia.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

events.text: The current constitution of Mexico is adopted, establishing a federal republic with powers separated into independent executive, legislative, and judicial branches.
The Congress of the United States passes the Immigration Act of 1917 over President Woodrow Wilson's veto.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

events.text: Stephen W. Thompson shoots down a German airplane; this is the first aerial victory by the U.S. military.
SS Tuscania is torpedoed off the coast of Ireland; it is the first ship carrying American troops to Europe to be torpedoed and sunk.
Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks, and D. W. Griffith launch United Artists.
Australian cricketer Bill Ponsford made 429 runs to break the world record for the highest first-class score.

main.desc: Team sport played with a bat and ball

events.text: The Royal Greenwich Observatory begins broadcasting the hourly time signals known as the Greenwich Time Signal.
Mutiny on Royal Netherlands Navy warship HNLMS De Zeven Provinciën off the coast of Sumatra, Dutch East Indies.
World War II: Allied forces begin the Battle of Keren to capture Keren, Eritrea.
World War II: General Douglas MacArthur returns to Manila.
After a mid-air collision with a fighter plane during a practice exercise off Tybee Island, Georgia, a U.S. Air Force bomber jettisoned a Mark 15 nuclear bomb, which was presumed lost.

main.desc: US Air Force incident involving a nuclear bomb

A hydrogen bomb known as the Tybee Bomb is lost by the US Air Force off the coast of Savannah, Georgia, never to be recovered.
French President Charles de Gaulle calls for Algeria to be granted independence.

links.t: Van Gend en Loos v Nederlandse Administratie der Belastingen
Direct effect of European Union law

main.desc: Period of sociopolitical turmoil in China (1966–1976)

main.desc: Period of sociopolitical turmoil in China (1966–1976)

events.text: Astronauts land on the Moon in the Apollo 14 mission.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Peru

events.text: Operation Soap: The Metropolitan Toronto Police Force raids four gay bathhouses in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, arresting just under 300, triggering mass protest and rallies.

main.desc: Police raid of gay bathhouses in Toronto, Canada

Ugo Vetere, then the mayor of Rome, and Chedli Klibi, then the mayor of Carthage, meet in Tunis to sign a treaty of friendship officially ending the Third Punic War which lasted 2,131 years.
Manuel Noriega is indicted on drug smuggling and money laundering charges.

main.desc: Military dictator of Panama from 1983 to 1989

main.desc: American white supremacist, Klansman, and convicted murderer

main.desc: 1994 bombardment of civilians in Sarajevo during the Bosnian War

events.text: The so-called Big Three banks in Switzerland announce the creation of a $71 million fund to aid Holocaust survivors and their families.

Russian forces massacre at least 60 civilians in the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, Chechnya.
The National Revolutionary Front for the Liberation of Haiti captured the city of Gonaïves, starting a coup d'état against President Jean-Bertrand Aristide's government.

main.t: National Revolutionary Front for the Liberation and Reconstruction of Haiti

main.t: National Revolutionary Front for the Liberation and Reconstruction of Haiti

A major tornado outbreak across the Southern United States kills 57.

main.desc: Deadly tornado outbreak in the southern United States

events.text: The United States Navy guided missile cruiser  Port Royal ran aground (pictured) on a coral reef off the island of Oahu.

main.desc: Maritime service branch of the U.S. military

links.t: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

main.desc: President of the United States (2017–2021; since 2025)

main.desc: Shahanshah of the Sasanian Empire from 579 to 590

James II of England and VII of Scotland is proclaimed King upon the death of his brother Charles II.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1685 to 1688

events.text: Dandara dos Palmares, leader of the runaway slaves in Quilombo dos Palmares, Brazil, is captured and commits suicide rather than be returned to a life of slavery.

main.desc: Establishment of Singapore as a British trading port

The first 86 African American immigrants sponsored by the American Colonization Society depart New York to start a settlement in present-day Liberia.

main.desc: Ethnic and cultural group in the United States

Signing of the Treaty of Waitangi, establishing New Zealand as a British colony.

main.desc: 19th- and 20th-century American form of musical theater

Union forces earned one of their first important victories in the American Civil War at the Battle of Fort Henry in western Tennessee.
American Civil War: Forces under the command of Ulysses S. Grant and Andrew H. Foote give the Union its first victory of the war, capturing Fort Henry, Tennessee in the Battle of Fort Henry.
Finland established its modern system of secular municipalities, separate from church parishes.

main.desc: Person refusing military service on moral grounds

Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments files the first patent for an integrated circuit.

At the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in China, a Long March 3B rocket carrying Intelsat 708 veers off course and crashes into a rural village after liftoff, killing somewhere between six and 100 people.
Then-Prime Minister of Canada Jean Chrétien applies a chokehold to protester Bill Clennett, an incident later named the Shawinigan Handshake.
Abdullah Öcalan, one of the founding members of the militant organization the Kurdistan Workers' Party, was arrested by Turkish security forces in Nairobi, Kenya.

main.desc: Founder of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK)

events.text: The first draft of the complete human genome is published in Nature.

main.desc: Complete set of nucleic acid sequences for humans

events.text: In one of the largest anti-war rallies in history, millions around the world in approximately 800 cities took part in protests against the impending invasion of Iraq.

main.desc: Social movement opposed to armed conflicts

events.text: Protests against the Iraq war take place in over 600 cities worldwide. It is estimated that between eight million and 30 million people participate, making this the largest peace demonstration in history.
The last Ariane 4 rocket is launched from the Guiana Space Centre, carrying Intelsat 907.
Two passenger trains collided in Halle, Belgium, when one driver failed to stop at a red signal, resulting in 19 deaths and 171 injuries.
Two trains collide in the Halle train collision in Halle, Belgium, killing 19 and injuring 171 people.
Three hundred and sixty people die in a fire at a Honduran prison in the city of Comayagua.
A meteor exploded (video featured) over Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia, producing a shock wave that injured about 1,500 people.

main.desc: Near-Earth asteroid that fell over Russia in 2013

events.text: A meteor explodes over Russia, injuring 1,500 people as a shock wave blows out windows and rocks buildings. This happens unexpectedly only hours before the expected closest ever approach of the larger and unrelated asteroid 2012 DA14.

main.desc: Near-Earth asteroid that fell over Russia in 2013

events.text: Following nationwide protests, Hailemariam Desalegn announced his resignation as prime minister of Ethiopia, remaining in post as a caretaker until he was succeeded by Abiy Ahmed.
Sixty people drown and hundreds are missing after a boat sinks on the Congo River near the village of Longola Ekoti, Mai-Ndombe Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
King Louis IX dispatched André de Longjumeau as the French ambassador to the Mongol Empire.
Andrew of Longjumeau is dispatched by Louis IX of France as his ambassador to meet with the Khagan of the Mongol Empire.
Livonian Crusade: In the Battle of Karuse, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania achieved a decisive victory over the Livonian Order on the frozen surface of the Baltic Sea.
The Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeats the Livonian Order in the Battle of Karuse.
Dutch forces led by Hendrick Lonck capture Olinda in what was to become part of Dutch Brazil.

main.desc: 16/17th-century Dutch sea captain and naval hero

events.text: Battle of Torrington, Devon: The last major battle of the First English Civil War.

main.desc: 1646 battle of the First English Civil War in Devon, England

events.text: First Leopoldine Diploma is issued by the Holy Roman Emperor, recognizing the Greek Catholic clergy enjoyed the same privileges as Roman Catholic priests in the Principality of Transylvania.
Spencer Compton, Earl of Wilmington, becomes British Prime Minister.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Great Britain from 1742 to 1743

links.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Colombo in Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) falls to the British, completing their invasion of Ceylon.

main.desc: Most populous city of Sri Lanka

events.text: First Barbary War: Lieutenant Stephen Decatur led a U.S. Navy raid to destroy the captured USS Philadelphia in the harbor of Tripoli (depicted), denying her use to the Barbary States.

main.desc: War between United States and the Barbary states, 1801–1805

events.text: First Barbary War: Stephen Decatur leads a raid to burn the pirate-held frigate USS Philadelphia.

main.desc: War between United States and the Barbary states, 1801–1805

events.text: The French government passed a law setting the musical note A4 to a frequency of 435 hertz, in the first attempt to standardize concert pitch.
American Civil War: A Union victory at the Battle of Fort Donelson gave General Ulysses S. Grant the nickname "Unconditional Surrender".
American Civil War: General Ulysses S. Grant captures Fort Donelson, Tennessee.
Spencer Compton Cavendish, Marquess of Hartington becomes British Secretary of State for War.
The Canadian Pacific Railway is incorporated by Act of Parliament at Ottawa (44th Vic., c.1).

main.desc: Class I railway in Canada and the United States

events.text: Iceland's first football club, Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur, is founded.

main.desc: Island country in the Atlantic Ocean

events.text: The Southern Cross Expedition led by Carsten Borchgrevink (pictured) achieved a new Farthest South of 78° 50'S, making the first landing at the Great Ice Barrier.
The Southern Cross expedition led by Carsten Borchgrevink achieves a new Farthest South of 78° 50'S, making the first landing at the Great Ice Barrier.
The Council of Lithuania signed the Act of Independence (pictured), proclaiming the restoration of an independent Lithuania.
The Council of Lithuania unanimously adopts the Act of Independence, declaring Lithuania an independent state.
A landslide in Byblos revealed a sarcophagus in an underground tomb that was later discovered to be part of a large Bronze Age necropolis.
Howard Carter unseals the burial chamber of Pharaoh Tutankhamun.
The Romanian Football Federation joins FIFA.

main.desc: Association football governing body in Romania

events.text: The Austrian Civil War ends with the defeat of the Social Democrats and the Republikanischer Schutzbund.

main.desc: 1934 civil war within the First Austrian Republic

events.text: The Commission of Government is officially sworn in; ending 79 years of responsible government in Newfoundland.

main.desc: 1934–1949 government of the Dominion of Newfoundland

events.text: The Popular Front, a coalition of left-wing parties, came to power in the Spanish general election, a factor in the outbreak of the Spanish Civil War five months later.

main.desc: Left-wing political party in the Second Spanish Republic from 1936 to 1939

events.text: The Popular Front wins the 1936 Spanish general election.
Wallace H. Carothers receives a United States patent for nylon.
World War II: Altmark incident: The German tanker Altmark is boarded by sailors from the British destroyer HMS Cossack. A total of 299 British prisoners are freed.
World War II: In Athens, the Greek People's Liberation Army is established

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Greece

events.text: World War II: Attack on Aruba, first World War II German shots fired on a land based object in the Americas.

main.desc: World War II battle in the Caribbean

events.text: World War II: In the early phases of the Third Battle of Kharkov, Red Army troops re-enter the city.

main.desc: 1943 series of battles on the Eastern Front of World War II

events.text: World War II: American forces land on Corregidor Island in the Philippines.

main.desc: WWII battle in the Pacific Theater

events.text: The Alaska Equal Rights Act of 1945, the first anti-discrimination law in the United States, was signed into law.

main.desc: First anti-discrimination state law in the U.S.

events.text: Fidel Castro was sworn in as Prime Minister of Cuba, beginning his decades-long rule over the country.
Fidel Castro becomes Premier of Cuba after dictator Fulgencio Batista was overthrown on January 1.
The U.S. Navy submarine USS Triton begins Operation Sandblast, setting sail from New London, Connecticut, to begin the first submerged circumnavigation of the globe.
The DuSable Museum, the first museum dedicated to the study and conservation of African American history, culture, and art, was chartered.
Explorer program: Explorer 9 (S-56a) is launched.
The Great Sheffield Gale impacts the United Kingdom, killing nine people; the city of Sheffield is devastated, with 150,000 homes damaged.
Flooding in the coastal areas of West Germany kills 315 and destroys the homes of about 60,000 people.

main.desc: Natural disaster affecting mainly the coastal regions of Germany

events.text: In Haleyville, Alabama, the first 9-1-1 emergency telephone system goes into service.
Civil Air Transport Flight 010 crashes near Shongshan Airport in Taiwan, killing 21 of the 63 people on board and one more on the ground.
The first computer bulletin board system is created (CBBS in Chicago).
The Ash Wednesday bushfires burned over half a million acres (over 2,000 km2) each in both South Australia and Victoria, killing 75 people and injuring 2,676 others.
The Ash Wednesday bushfires in Victoria and South Australia kill 75.
Iran launches Operation Dawn 5, a major offensive during the Iran–Iraq War targeting the Basra–Baghdad highway, resulting in heavy casualties on both sides.
The Lebanese Shia political and paramilitary organization Hezbollah released a manifesto describing its ideology and goals.
Hezbollah is founded.

main.desc: Islamist movement and militant group based in Lebanon

events.text: The Soviet liner MS Mikhail Lermontov runs aground in the Marlborough Sounds, New Zealand.
China Airlines Flight 2265 crashes into the Pacific Ocean near Penghu Airport in Taiwan, killing all 13 aboard.
Nicaraguan Contras leader Enrique Bermúdez is assassinated in Managua.
Eleven people died in a train collision in Silver Spring, Maryland, leading to the creation of comprehensive U.S. federal rules for the design of passenger cars.

main.desc: Fatal train crash in the United States

events.text: A Chicago-bound Amtrak train, the Capitol Limited, collides with a MARC commuter train bound for Washington, D.C., killing 11 people.
While on approach to Chiang Kai-shek International Airport, China Airlines Flight 676 crashed due to an over-reliance of the autopilot, which resulted in the deaths of 202 people.

main.desc: Main airport serving Taoyuan and Taipei, Taiwan

events.text: China Airlines Flight 676 crashes into a road and residential area near Chiang Kai-shek International Airport in Taiwan, killing all 196 aboard and six more on the ground.
Emery Worldwide Airlines Flight 17 crashes near Sacramento Mather Airport in Rancho Cordova, California, killing all three aboard.
The Kyoto Protocol comes into force, following its ratification by Russia.

main.desc: 1997 international treaty to reduce greenhouse gas emissions

events.text: The National Hockey League cancels the entire 2004–05 regular season and playoffs.

main.desc: North American professional ice hockey league

events.text: The last Mobile army surgical hospital (MASH) is decommissioned by the United States Army.

main.desc: Decommissioned type of U.S. Army medical unit

events.text: At least 91 people were killed and 190 others injured after a bomb hidden in a water tank exploded at a market in Hazara Town, Pakistan.
A bomb blast at a market in Hazara Town, Quetta, Pakistan kills more than 80 people and injures 190 others.

Five thousand people gathered in the town of Kherrata, Bejaia Province to mark the second anniversary of the Hirak protest movement. Demonstrations had been suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria.
Northern Crusades: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Teutonic Knights meet in the Battle of Rudau.

main.desc: 12th- and 13th-century crusades around the Baltic Sea

events.text: Following the successful campaigns during the Ottoman Interregnum, Musa Çelebi, one of the sons of Bayezid I, becomes Sultan of the Ottoman Empire with the support of Mircea I of Wallachia.

main.desc: Civil war in the early 15th century Ottoman Empire

events.text: Duke Frederick of Schleswig-Holstein and King John of Denmark attempt to subdue the peasantry of Dithmarschen, Denmark, in the Battle of Hemmingstedt.
On his way to be burned at the stake for heresy, at Campo de' Fiori in Rome, the philosopher Giordano Bruno has a wooden vise put on his tongue to prevent him continuing to speak.
Nurhaci proclaims himself Khan of the Later Jin, precursor to the Qing Dynasty.

main.desc: Founding khan of the Later Jin dynasty

links.t: List of emperors of the Qing dynasty

events.text: Myles Standish was elected the first commander of the militia of Plymouth Colony.
Myles Standish is appointed as first military commander of the English Plymouth Colony in North America.
An earthquake strikes the Indonesian island of Ambon. It triggers a 100 m (330 ft) megatsunami which drowns over 2,300 people.
Sixteen men of Pascual de Iriate's expedition are lost at Evangelistas Islets at the western end of the Strait of Magellan.
The Battle of Vasai commences as the Marathas move to invade Portuguese-occupied territory.

main.desc: 1739 conflict between the Portuguese and Maratha Empires in India

events.text: In Sweden, February 17 is followed by March 1 as the country moves from the Julian calendar to the Gregorian calendar.

United States presidential election: A tie in the Electoral College between Thomas Jefferson and Aaron Burr is resolved when Jefferson is elected President of the United States and Burr Vice President by the United States House of Representatives.

links.t: Vice President of the United States

events.text: War of the Sixth Coalition: The Battle of Mormant.
The United States ratifies the Treaty of Ghent – signed in late 1814 – formally ending the War of 1812.

main.desc: 1814 peace treaty ending the War of 1812

events.text: The United States House of Representatives passes the Missouri Compromise for the first time.

main.desc: Lower house of the U.S. Congress

events.text: Great Trek: Zulu impis massacred about 532 Voortrekkers, Khoekhoe, and Basuto near present-day Weenen, South Africa.

main.desc: 1836–1852 Boer migrations away from the British Cape Colony

events.text: In the Weenen massacre, hundreds of Voortrekkers along the Blaukraans River, Natal are killed by Zulus.

main.desc: 1838 massacre in present-day Weenen, South Africa

events.text: The United Kingdom recognizes the independence of the Orange Free State.
Cochinchina campaign: French Navy forces captured the Citadel of Saigon, defended by 1,000 Vietnamese soldiers of the Nguyễn dynasty.
Cochinchina Campaign: The French Navy captures the Citadel of Saigon, a fortress manned by 1,000 Nguyễn dynasty soldiers, en route to conquering Saigon and other regions of southern Viet Nam.
A group of citizens of Geneva found an International Committee for Relief to the Wounded, which later became known as the International Committee of the Red Cross.

links.t: International Committee of the Red Cross

events.text: American Civil War: The H. L. Hunley becomes the first submarine to engage and sink a warship, the USS Housatonic.
American Civil War: Columbia, South Carolina, is burned as Confederate forces flee from advancing Union forces.

main.desc: Capital city of South Carolina, United States

events.text: Rudolf Diesel's first working diesel engine ran for one minute.
Italian composer Giacomo Puccini's Madama Butterfly  premiered at La Scala in Milan to poor reviews, forcing him to revise the opera.
Russian Revolution of 1905: Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia is assassinated in the Moscow Kremlin by Socialist Revolutionary Ivan Kalyayev.

main.desc: Political and social unrest in the Russian Empire

links.t: Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia

events.text: The Armory Show (commemorative button pictured), the first large modern-art exhibition in the United States, opened at the 69th Regiment Armory in New York City.
The Armory Show opens in New York City, displaying works of artists who subsequently become some of the most influential painters of the early 20th century.
The Ukrainian People's Republic asks the Entente and the United States for help fighting the Bolsheviks.
World War II: The U.S. Navy began Operation Hailstone, a massive naval air and surface attack against the Japanese naval and air base at Chuuk Lagoon in the Caroline Islands.
World War II: The Battle of Eniwetok begins. The battle ends in an American victory on February 22.
World War II: Operation Hailstone begins: U.S. naval air, surface and submarine attack against Truk Lagoon, Japan's main base in the central Pacific, in support of the Eniwetok invasion.

main.desc: American attack on Truk Lagoon during World War II

events.text: The Al-Waziri coup briefly ousts the ruling Hamidaddin dynasty of Yemen; Imam Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din is killed.

main.desc: 1948 conflict in the Kingdom of Yemen

events.text: Chaim Weizmann begins his term as the first President of Israel.
Vanguard 2 (model pictured), the first weather satellite, was launched to measure cloud cover distribution.
Project Vanguard: Vanguard 2: The first weather satellite is launched to measure cloud-cover distribution.

main.desc: U.S. Navy satellite program in the 1950s

events.text: A Turkish Airlines Vickers Viscount crashes near Gatwick Airport, killing 14; Turkish prime minister Adnan Menderes survives the crash.
Gabonese military officers overthrew President Léon M'ba, but French forces, honouring a 1960 treaty, forcibly reinstated him two days later.

main.desc: Military coup against President Léon M'ba

events.text: In Wesberry v. Sanders the Supreme Court of the United States rules that congressional districts have to be approximately equal in population.

main.desc: 1964 United States Supreme Court case on congressional districts

links.t: Supreme Court of the United States
List of United States congressional districts

events.text: Gabonese president Léon M'ba is toppled by a coup and his rival, Jean-Hilaire Aubame, is installed in his place.

main.desc: Prime Minister (1959–61) and President (1961–67) of Gabon

events.text: Project Ranger: The Ranger 8 probe launches on its mission to photograph the Mare Tranquillitatis region of the Moon in preparation for the crewed Apollo missions. Mare Tranquillitatis or the "Sea of Tranquility" would become the site chosen for the Apollo 11 lunar landing.

main.desc: American uncrewed lunar space missions in the 1960s

events.text: Aeroflot Flight 065 crashes during take-off from Sheremetyevo International Airport, killing 21.
American aquanaut Berry L. Cannon dies of carbon dioxide poisoning while attempting to repair a leak in the SEALAB III underwater habitat. The SEALAB project was subsequently abandoned.

main.desc: American aquanaut who died in a diving incident (1935–1969)

events.text: The family of Jeffrey R. MacDonald, United States Army captain, is found murdered in their home in Fort Bragg, North Carolina, US. Eventually, MacDonald was charged with and convicted of the murder of his pregnant wife and two daughters.

main.desc: American military physician convicted of murder (born 1943)

events.text: Cumulative sales of the Volkswagen Beetle exceed those of the Ford Model T.
A U.S. Army soldier stole a Bell UH-1 helicopter (pictured) and landed it on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, D.C.

main.desc: Huey family of American military utility helicopters

events.text: Robert K. Preston, a disgruntled U.S. Army private, buzzes the White House in a stolen helicopter.

main.desc: Theft and flight of military aircraft

events.text: The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army carried out a bombing of a restaurant near Belfast, Northern Ireland, killing twelve people and injuring thirty others.
The Troubles: The Provisional IRA detonates an incendiary bomb at the La Mon restaurant, near Belfast, killing 12 and seriously injuring 30 others, all Protestants.
The Sino-Vietnamese War begins.

main.desc: War between China and Vietnam in 1979

events.text: First winter ascent of Mount Everest by Krzysztof Wielicki and Leszek Cichy.
Ryan International Airlines Flight 590 crashes during takeoff from Cleveland Hopkins International Airport, killing both pilots, the aircraft's only occupants.
First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Armenian troops massacre more than 20 Azerbaijani civilians during the Capture of Garadaghly.
The Cenepa War between Peru and Ecuador ends on a ceasefire brokered by the UN.

main.desc: Brief territorial conflict between Ecuador and Peru in early 1995

events.text: An earthquake with a moment magnitude of 8.2 and a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent) occurred in the New Guinea Trench, which generated a tsunami that killed 108 people.

main.desc: Earthquake and tsunami in eastern Indonesia

events.text: In Philadelphia, world champion Garry Kasparov beats the Deep Blue supercomputer in a chess match.

main.desc: Most populous city in Pennsylvania, US

events.text: NASA's Discovery Program begins as the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft lifts off on the first mission ever to orbit and land on an asteroid, 433 Eros.

The 8.2 Mw Biak earthquake shakes the Papua province of eastern Indonesia with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). A large tsunami followed, leaving 166 people dead or missing and 423 injured.

main.desc: Earthquake and tsunami in eastern Indonesia

events.text: A massive mudslide occurs in Southern Leyte, Philippines; the official death toll is set at 1,126.
Kosovo declares independence from Serbia.

Arab Spring: Bahraini security forces killed four protesters in a pre-dawn raid at the Pearl Roundabout in Manama, while the "Day of Rage" took place in Libya with nationwide protests against Muammar Gaddafi's government.

main.desc: 2010s protests and revolutions in the Arab world

events.text: Arab Spring: Libyan protests against Muammar Gaddafi's regime begin.

main.desc: 2010s protests and revolutions in the Arab world

links.t: History of Libya under Muammar Gaddafi

events.text: Arab Spring: In Bahrain, security forces launch a deadly pre-dawn raid on protesters in Pearl Roundabout in Manama; the day is locally known as Bloody Thursday.
Eighteen people are killed and 78 injured in a stampede at a Mardi Gras parade in Haiti.

main.desc: Human stampede at a Mardi Gras parade in Haiti

events.text: Military vehicles explode outside a Turkish Armed Forces barracks in Ankara, Turkey, killing at least 29 people and injuring 61 others.

main.desc: Bombing in Turkey by Kurdish separatists

events.text: According to Hindu scriptures, Kali Yuga, the last of the four stages that the world goes through as part of the cycle of yugas, began.
Kali Yuga, the fourth and final yuga of Hinduism, starts with the death of Krishna.

main.desc: Last of four yugas (ages) in Hindu cosmology

events.text: The Sixth Crusade: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor, signs a ten-year truce with al-Kamil, regaining Jerusalem, Nazareth, and Bethlehem with neither military engagements nor support from the papacy.

main.desc: 1228–1229 attempted conquest of the Holy Land

events.text: Northern Crusades: The Battle of Wesenberg (depicted) took place between Novgorodian and Pskovian forces against the Livonian Order and its allies, ending with Russian forces retreating from Danish Estonia.

main.desc: 12th- and 13th-century crusades around the Baltic Sea

events.text: The Battle of Wesenberg is fought between the Livonian Order and Dovmont of Pskov.
Amda Seyon I, Emperor of Ethiopia begins his campaigns in the southern Muslim provinces.
Eighty Years' War: Off the coast of Cornwall, a Spanish fleet intercepted an Anglo-Dutch merchant convoy of forty-four vessels escorted by six men-of-war, destroying or capturing twenty ships.
Eighty Years' War: Off the coast of Cornwall, England, a Spanish fleet intercepts an important Anglo-Dutch merchant convoy of 44 vessels escorted by six warships, destroying or capturing 20 of them.
The ballad opera called Flora, or Hob in the Well went down in history as the first opera of any kind to be produced in North America (Charleston, S.C.)

Enslaved Malagasy captives on the Dutch East India Company slave ship Meermin began a mutiny that led to the ship's destruction on Cape Agulhas in present-day South Africa and the recapture of the instigators.
Fourth Anglo-Dutch War: Captain Thomas Shirley opens his expedition against Dutch colonial outposts on the Gold Coast of Africa (present-day Ghana).

main.desc: War between Great Britain and Dutch Republic, 1780–1784

events.text: Congress passes a law admitting the state of Vermont to the Union, effective 4 March, after that state had existed for 14 years as a de facto independent largely unrecognized state.

main.desc: Process of states joining the United States

events.text: French Revolutionary Wars: Sir Ralph Abercromby and a fleet of 18 British warships invade Trinidad.

Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Montereau.

main.desc: 1803–1815 series of wars led by Napoleon

events.text: In Montgomery, Alabama, Jefferson Davis is inaugurated as the provisional President of the Confederate States of America.

main.desc: Capital city of Alabama, United States

events.text: With Italian unification almost complete, Victor Emmanuel II of Piedmont, Savoy and Sardinia assumes the title of King of Italy.
Vasil Levski, a national hero of Bulgaria, was executed in Sofia by the Ottoman authorities for his efforts to establish an independent Bulgarian republic.
Bulgarian revolutionary leader Vasil Levski is executed by hanging in Sofia by the Ottoman authorities.
Competition between two American merchants in Lincoln County, New Mexico Territory, turned into a range war when a member of one faction was murdered by the other.

main.desc: County in New Mexico, United States

events.text: John Tunstall is murdered by outlaw Jesse Evans, sparking the Lincoln County War in Lincoln County, New Mexico.
Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain is published in the United States.
Second Boer War: Imperial forces suffer their worst single-day loss of life on Bloody Sunday, the first day of the Battle of Paardeberg.
Édouard de Laveleye forms the Belgian Olympic Committee in Brussels.

main.desc: Service which transports mail by air

links.t: United Provinces of Agra and Oudh
Presidencies and provinces of British India

main.desc: WWI German naval campaign to attack Allied trade routes (1914–18)

events.text: While studying photographs taken in January, Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto.

main.desc: 1st month in the Julian and Gregorian calendars

main.desc: First cow to fly in an airplane

The core members of the White Rose, an anti-Nazi resistance group, were arrested by the Gestapo.
World War II: The Nazis arrest the members of the White Rose movement.
World War II: Joseph Goebbels delivers his Sportpalast speech.

World War II: American and Brazilian troops kick off Operation Encore in Northern Italy, a successful limited action in the Northern Apennines that prepares for the western portion of the Allied Spring offensive.

main.desc: 1945 Allied offensive in World War II

events.text: President Harry S. Truman signed the Rescission Act, annulling benefits payable to Filipino troops who fought for the U.S. during World War II.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1945 to 1953

links.t: Presidencies and provinces of British India

events.text: First Indochina War: The French gain complete control of Hanoi after forcing the Viet Minh to withdraw to the mountains.
The first Church of Scientology is established in Los Angeles.

Kenyan rebel leader Dedan Kimathi is executed by the British colonial government.
Walter James Bolton becomes the last person legally executed in New Zealand.
The Gambia becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
The Chicago Seven are found not guilty of conspiring to incite riots at the 1968 Democratic National Convention.
The California Supreme Court in the case of People v. Anderson, (6 Cal.3d 628) invalidates the state's death penalty and commutes the sentences of all death row inmates to life imprisonment.

main.desc: Highest judicial court in the U.S. state of California

events.text: NASA's first Space Shuttle, Enterprise, made its first test flight on top of the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft (both pictured).
The Xinjiang 61st Regiment Farm fire started during Chinese New Year when a firecracker ignited the wreaths of late Mao Zedong, killing 694 personnel.

List of fireworks accidents and incidents

The Space Shuttle Enterprise test vehicle is carried on its maiden "flight" on top of a Boeing 747.

main.desc: Space Shuttle test vehicle, used for glide tests

main.desc: 1983 mass shooting and robbery in Seattle

events.text: The IRA explodes bombs in the early morning at Paddington station and Victoria station in London.

links.t: Bombings of Paddington and Victoria stations

FBI agent Robert Hanssen is arrested for spying for the Soviet Union. He is ultimately convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment.

Sampit conflict: Inter-ethnic violence between Dayaks and Madurese breaks out in Sampit, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, ultimately resulting in more than 500 deaths and 100,000 Madurese displaced from their homes.

main.desc: 2001 inter-ethnic violence throughout Central Kalimantan, Indonesia

events.text: 192 people die when an arsonist sets fire to a subway train in Daegu, South Korea.

main.desc: 2003 subway arson in Daegu, South Korea

main.desc: City in Razavi Khorasan Province, Iran
